scope_note: US-market Dodge Durango, all trims (R/T, Citadel, SRT/SRT 392, SRT Hellcat, R/T 392, 2009 HEMI Hybrid). 2WD/RWD and 4WD/AWD treated as one model. Independent-source groups: Dodge/Chrysler/FCA/Stellantis media = one; Wikipedia = one; EPA (size/cylinders only), Consumer Guide, KBB, MotorWeek, Auto123, Autotrader.ca, Guide Auto Web, The Truth About Cars each one. NHRA input file was empty, so nhra=false throughout. HP is SAE net. No source used states Chrysler sales codes (EZH, ERB etc.), so rpo holds engine family names only.
notes: Production gap: no 2010 model year. Newark Assembly ended second-generation production on Dec 19, 2008 (last MY 2009); the third generation launched as a 2011 model.
1998: 4WD V8 only (EPA). The 3.9 V6 named in 1998 launch coverage appeared for 1999 only; recorded as excluded_not_produced for 1998.
Shelby S.P.360 (1999-2000) is a dealer-sold conversion, not a factory engine.
2022: no SRT Hellcat. 2025: no 6.4 (SRT 392 dropped; lineup GT / R/T / SRT Hellcat). 2026: 6.4 returns as R/T 392; 5.7 becomes GT HEMI; V-6 dropped Aug 2025, then reinstated Nov 2025.
Not recorded: 2027 model year (announced by Dodge; outside scope). Police Special Service Durango (2014+) uses the same 3.6/5.7 engines.
